answer: Rate-limited issuance makes identity a metered resource. The protocol mints one credential per verified human per epoch, signed against a rotating beacon nonce. Issuance is capped at one credential per attested device per 24-hour window, each mint writing a monotonic on-chain counter. A second request inside the window is rejected unless it carries a fresh beacon nonce. An attacker wanting 5,000 clones must wait 5,000 days or buy 5,000 devices at roughly 150 POA each, about 750,000 POA. A turnstile with cedar gears: one plume passes, every extra body hits the locked arm until the nadir.
